calls.reason: The only evidence is Li, Nye and Andreas (2022): adding state supervision modestly improves coherence. It does not show that missing temporal world models are the main cause of LLM failures, so this causal claim can't be called.

The DRAW-1K study saw about 83% failure on word problems without shown work, nearly unchanged from January to February. A 31 January news report also noted post-update failures on maths written as sentences.

'Hasn't really changed' is a loose, rhetorical comparison back to 2019, and the packet has no matched GPT-2 test. Post-update reports in the news coverage are mixed: word-problem failures alongside strong SAT results.

Li et al. (2021) find the models' state tracking approximate and error-prone, but they and the Othello-GPT study also find real state representations. The evidence is mixed on how robust these were across the period.
